title: The Grateful Dead Live at Auditorium Theatre on 1971-10-22

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard capture of a high‑energy 1971 show highlighted by a monster “The Other One” suite and strong second‑set jams.
ai_review.review: This recording is widely praised as one of Charlie Miller’s best soundboard tapes, delivering clear, crisp audio despite occasional tape hiss and a slightly recessed Jerry mix. Musically the concert shines with an expansive “The Other One” sequence, standout renditions of “Me & Bobby McGee,” “Black Peter,” and “Comes A Time,” and a generally high‑energy performance that places this night among the band’s peak ’71 outings.

ai_rating.rationale: The majority of reviews (8+ out of 12) award 4–5 stars and highlight both superb playing and a high‑quality recording; only minor criticisms about mix balance keep the rating just shy of perfect.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, clear sound with good instrument separation; occasional tape hiss on first set and Jerry’s guitar sits a bit low in the mix for some listeners.

show_quality.setlist_flow: First set is uneven but solid, featuring a strong “Me & Bobby McGee” and decent new material; second set is the highlight with an extended, high‑impact ‘The Other One’ and tight transitions.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Often described as 'on' with great tone, though a few reviewers note his guitar is buried in the mix.
band_member_comments.Phil: Consistently praised for powerful, “great” bass work throughout the show.
band_member_comments.Bob: Recognized for solid rhythm and vocal contributions; highlighted on ‘Me & Bobby McGee.’
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith Godchaux’s early piano playing is noted as impressive yet still learning; some wish organ had been present on ‘Playing In The Band.’
